==Problem==
Elijah has a large collection of identical wooden cubes which are white on 
4 faces and gray on 
2 faces that share an edge. He glues some cubes together face-to-face. The figure below shows 
2 cubes being glued together, leaving 
3 gray faces visible. What is the fewest number of cubes that he could glue together to ensure that no gray faces are visible, no matter how he rotates the figure?

[[File:2026 amc 8 q15.png | 650px]]

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 4 \qquad\textbf{(B)}\ 6 \qquad\textbf{(C)}\ 8 \qquad\textbf{(D)}\ 9 \qquad\textbf{(E)}\ 27</imath>

==Solution 1 (2D Plane)==

Create a square in which two adjecent sides are colored red. Now, connect each of <imath>n</imath> squares such that each red side is tangent to another. What is the minimum number required?

By solving this bijection, we solve the problem above. Through experimentation, each square, assuming the colored sides are the rightmost and bottom of a square, must have another square on the side and below. Thus we obtain 3 squares.

However, the top right square must have one more square below it, giving us a final count of <imath>3+1 = \boxed{4}</imath> minimum cubes.

~Pinotation

==Solution 2 (omg so easy)==

We can have <imath>4</imath> cubes with all their gray faces facing each other, and that will make no gray faces visible. Therefore, our answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(A)}\ 4}</imath>. Note that this is also the minimum answer choice.

~Yuhao2012, Baihly2024

==Solution 3==
Every time we add a new cube, there are <imath>2</imath> colored faces that are added, but only <imath>1</imath> colored face on <imath>2</imath> cubes that are covered. If we start with <imath>1</imath> cube, we see adding another cube colored-on-colored can cause both remaining colored faces to face in the same direction. So if we have <imath>2</imath>  <imath>2</imath> x <imath>1</imath> cube formations, by aligning all of the colored faces onto one plane we get the minimum of <imath>\boxed{4}</imath>. That is pretty nice beccause we won't have any doubts about whether it could be lower.

~Blue_kite, although it was pretty obvious.
